## Typo Tolerance

When a customer misspells a product name, the search should still find what they were looking for. Right now, the site treats a misspelled word as if it simply does not exist — returning a blank page instead of the closest matching products. For a specialty outdoor retailer where product names like "Imprägnierung" or "Reparaturmaterial" are genuinely difficult to spell, this is a direct path to lost sales.

**"Wanderhozen"** — a common phonetic misspelling of "Wanderhosen" (hiking pants) — returned nothing at all, even though the store carries a full range of hiking pants. A customer who types this and sees a blank page has no reason to try again.

The problem extends beyond typos to accidental spacing errors. When customers typed **"Wanderho sen"**, **"Pullov er"**, or **"Reparaturma terial"** — words broken at an arbitrary point, the kind of thing that happens on a mobile keyboard — the search again returned nothing. These are not exotic edge cases; they are the normal output of a touchscreen keyboard, and the store currently has no way to recover from them.

## Shopping Context

Customers often search the way they think about their needs — "something for autumn", "a winter expedition", "a spring run" — rather than using the exact category names the site uses internally. When the search cannot bridge that gap, it returns nothing even though the right products are sitting in the catalogue.

**"Windweste"** — a common regional term for a wind-protection vest — returned zero results. The store carries wind vests filed under "Windschutz-Westen", but the search has no connection between the two terms, so a customer using the everyday word hits a dead end.

**"Unterleibchen"** — a regional Swiss term for a base-layer top or undershirt — also returned nothing, even though the store stocks a full underwear and base-layer range under "Unterwäsche". The customer's word and the store's category label simply never meet.

In each case, the engine tried to match both words literally at the same time, found no product title containing both, and gave up rather than treating the season word as context and searching for the product type.

## Filters & Constraints

When a customer adds a price limit or a colour to their search, they expect those constraints to be respected. Right now, the search ignores both types of constraint entirely — treating price phrases as literal text to match against product names, and colour words as optional hints rather than requirements.

Every price-anchored query in this audit returned zero results. **"Hardshell-Hose unter 200 CHF"** Found nothing, even though the store stocks hardshell pants at a range of price points. **"Fleecepullover bis 100 CHF"** Returned nothing, despite fleece pullovers being available under that price. **"Wärmeweste unter 150 Franken"** — using the colloquial word "Franken" for Swiss francs — also returned nothing. **"Wanderhose unter 150 CHF"** Was the same. In every case, the engine tried to find the phrase "unter 200 CHF" or "bis 100 CHF" as literal text inside a product name, found nothing, and returned a blank page. The price constraint was never extracted and applied as a filter.

## Prioritized Roadmap

1. **Fix typo tolerance and word-splitting so misspelled or broken queries return results**
The search currently returns a blank page for any query with a misspelling ("Wanderhozen", "Pullofer", "Reperaturmaterial", "Imprägnirung"), an accidental mid-word space ("Wanderho sen", "Pullov er"), or an unrecognised special character ("Pull+over") — covering the Typo Tolerance capability across all critical failures. The engine needs to apply approximate matching so that queries within one or two characters of a real product term are automatically corrected before the search runs.
Impact: Critical | Effort: Medium Effort

2. **Require the product-type word to match, and weight it above all other terms**
Across Brand & Model Search, Product Discovery, and Language Understanding, the same defect recurs: the engine drops the head noun ("Pullover", "Weste", "Fleecejacke") and matches only on a modifier (gender token "W", material "Windstopper", brand "alpibreak"), filling the page with the wrong product type or burying the best match deep in the results. "W Pullover" returned mostly T-shirts; "Fleecejacke" put "Quad Merino Fleece Jacket" at position #9 behind generic jackets scoring half as high; "Windstopper Weste" included jackets where vests were requested. The fix is to treat the product-type noun as a required match and apply a strong title-field boost so that products containing that exact term in their name always rank above products that only share a secondary attribute.
Impact: Critical | Effort: Medium Effort

3. **Parse price phrases in search queries and apply them as filters**
All four price-anchored queries ("Hardshell-Hose unter 200 CHF", "Fleecepullover bis 100 CHF", "Wärmeweste unter 150 Franken", "Wanderhose unter 150 CHF") returned zero results because the engine tried to match the price phrase as literal product-title text. The search needs to detect patterns like "unter X CHF", "bis X CHF", and "unter X Franken", extract the price ceiling, and apply it as a catalogue filter — then run the remaining product-type term as the actual search query.
Impact: Critical | Effort: Medium Effort

4. **Map everyday and regional category terms to the correct catalogue categories**
Searches for "Windweste", "Unterleibchen", and "Thermounterwäsche" all returned zero results because the engine has no connection between these common terms and the store's internal category labels ("Windschutz-Westen", "Unterwäsche"). The same gap affects seasonal combinations like "Winterhose Expedition", "Sommershirt Trailrunning", and "Frühling Softshellweste", where the season word is treated as a required literal match rather than context. A synonym and intent map needs to be built so that these terms route to the right category and surface the products that are already in stock.
Impact: Critical | Effort: Medium Effort

5. **Treat brand + product-type combinations as an AND query with a graceful fallback**
"alpibreak Jacke" and "Kraszewski Weste" both returned zero results because the engine could not reconcile a brand token with a product-category token when no exact title overlap existed. When a brand name is present in a query alongside a product type, the engine should first attempt to return products from that brand in that category; if none exist, it should return the brand's full product range with a clear message, rather than a blank page.
Impact: Critical | Effort: Medium Effort

6. **Enforce colour and attribute constraints as filters, not optional hints**
For "Sport-BH schwarz", the colour word "schwarz" was ignored as a filter: many results were not black, and the two highest-scoring items ("Motion Bra", "Active Momentum 5529") were placed at positions #6 and #9 while lower-scoring items led the page. Colour and material attributes extracted from a query should be applied as a hard filter or a strong boosting signal so that products explicitly matching the stated attribute rank above those that do not.
Impact: Moderate | Effort: Quick Win

7. **Collapse product variants into a single result card per model**
For "HS Hose", "Nordwand Pro HS Pants W" appeared three times as separate colour and size variant cards, consuming three of nine result slots and hiding other distinct products. Variants of the same model should be grouped into one card, with colour and size selectable on the product page, so customers see the broadest possible range of distinct products in the results.
Impact: Minor | Effort: Medium Effort
